subjective.unit: Chief Complaint: Back pain and pins and needles in the right foot.
subjective.citation_text: Doctor: Hello. Could you tell me your age and gender, and what brings you in today? Patient: I'm 38 years old and male. I came in because my back started hurting after I was raking leaves yesterday, and I've been having some pins and needles in my right foot ever since. It's been bothering me a lot, and my partner is here because they've noticed it hurts more when I stand up. Doctor: Can you describe the nature of the back pain (e.g., sharp, dull, constant, intermittent), whether it radiates to other areas, and if there are any associated symptoms such as numbness, weakness, or changes in bowel or bladder function? Patient: The pain is more of a tightening feeling in my back, and it's been constant since it started. It doesn't radiate too much, but I do have some pins and needles in my right foot. There's no numbness or weakness that I can tell, and nothing wrong with my bowel or bladder function. Doctor: Have you experienced any prior episodes of back pain or neurological symptoms in the lower extremities? Do you have a history of back surgery, trauma, or conditions such as diabetes or spinal stenosis? Patient: I don't have a history of back pain or neurological symptoms in my lower extremities, and I don't have a history of back surgery, trauma, diabetes, or spinal stenosis. This seems to be the first time I've had an issue like this. Doctor: Could you please describe any neurological examination findings, such as reflexes, muscle strength, or sensory changes in your lower extremities? Patient: The doctor asked me to describe any neurological examination findings, like reflexes, muscle strength, or sensory changes in my lower extremities. I wasn't sure how to explain it, but I mentioned that I had some tingling in my right foot and that my partner noticed I had more pain when I stood up. I didn't really know about reflexes or muscle strength, so I just told them what I felt and what my partner saw
